title: Preparations for Full Metal Crowns — Test

mcqs.q: Which is another name for the full metal crown?
mcqs.explain: It is variously called the complete cast crown, full metal crown, casted crown or all-metal crown.

mcqs.q: Compared with other types of FULL crown, the full metal crown is:
mcqs.explain: It is conservative relative to other full crowns (which need more reduction for porcelain), though destructive compared with partial coverage.

mcqs.q: Which is an ADVANTAGE of the full metal crown?
opts: Less wear of the opposing natural teeth than porcelain
Requires less reduction than a partial-coverage crown
mcqs.explain: Metal is kinder to the opposing dentition than porcelain. Its drawbacks are esthetics, greater destruction than partial coverage, and galvanic/thermal conductivity.

mcqs.q: Which is a DISADVANTAGE of the complete cast crown?
opts: Galvanic and thermal conductivity can occur
mcqs.explain: Disadvantages are esthetics, being destructive compared with partial coverage, and galvanic/thermal conductivity — its strength, retention and margin adaptation are all good.

mcqs.q: The full metal crown is the restoration of choice whenever:
opts: Maximum retention and resistance are needed
Esthetics is the patient's main concern
A more conservative option would meet the objectives
mcqs.explain: It gives more retention and resistance than partial coverage and other full crowns — e.g. as a bridge retainer or on a short clinical crown.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT an indication for a full metal crown?
opts: Esthetics is the patient's primary concern
Extensive coronal destruction by caries or trauma
An inclined tooth that cannot be corrected
mcqs.explain: Esthetic priority is a contraindication; so is the situation where treatment objectives can be met with a more conservative restoration.

mcqs.q: A 'survey crown with an occlusal rest seat' is an indication that relates to:
opts: Providing guiding planes/rests for a removable partial denture
mcqs.explain: A survey crown is contoured to provide the undercuts, guiding planes and rest seats required by a removable partial denture.

mcqs.q: The minimum occlusal clearance required on the FUNCTIONAL (centric) cusps is:
mcqs.explain: 1.5 mm on functional (centric) cusps and 1 mm on non-functional (non-centric) cusps.

mcqs.q: The minimum occlusal clearance required on the NON-FUNCTIONAL (non-centric) cusps is:
mcqs.explain: 1 mm on non-functional cusps; the absolute minimum clearance quoted for the non-functional cusp is 0.6 mm.

mcqs.q: Occlusal reduction should follow the normal anatomic contours in order to:
opts: Remain as conservative as possible while giving uniform clearance
mcqs.explain: Following the anatomy provides uniform material thickness without removing unnecessary tooth structure.

mcqs.q: Axial reduction for a complete cast crown should provide a taper (convergence) of about:
mcqs.explain: A 6-degree total occlusal convergence balances retention with a path of draw free of undercuts.

mcqs.q: The margin configuration of choice for a full metal crown is a:
opts: Knife edge on the functional cusp
Bevelled shoulder with a metal collar
mcqs.explain: A smooth, distinct chamfer placed supragingivally where possible, giving about 0.5 mm of metal thickness at the margin.

mcqs.q: The chamfer should allow approximately how much metal thickness at the margin?
mcqs.explain: About 0.5 mm of metal at the margin — the chamfer must be smooth and distinct.

mcqs.q: The minimum chamfer width in a MOLAR is:
mcqs.explain: Minimum 0.5 mm in a molar; it can be less in a premolar.

mcqs.q: The purpose of the functional (centric) cusp bevel is to:
opts: Provide adequate bulk of metal where occlusal load is greatest
mcqs.explain: A wide bevel on the functional cusp ensures sufficient metal thickness on the cusp that carries centric contact, preventing perforation of the casting.

mcqs.q: Which instrument is NOT part of the stated armamentarium for a complete cast crown preparation?
opts: Flat-end tapered carbide for a shoulder
mcqs.explain: The armamentarium is two round-end tapered diamonds and a short needle diamond — a flat-end instrument would cut a shoulder, which is not the margin of choice here.

mcqs.q: The short needle diamond is particularly useful for:
opts: Proximal access without damaging the adjacent tooth
mcqs.explain: Its slim form breaks proximal contact and refines narrow areas safely.

mcqs.q: Which step comes FIRST in the preparation sequence?
opts: Axial reduction of the buccal wall
mcqs.explain: Depth-orientation grooves are cut into the inclined planes first so the subsequent occlusal reduction is measured and follows the anatomy.

mcqs.q: During axial reduction the chamfer is:
opts: Carried along as the axial wall is reduced, with the round-end tapered diamond
Cut last with a flat-end bur only
Omitted if the crown is supragingival
mcqs.explain: The round end of the tapered diamond creates the chamfer simultaneously with axial reduction, producing a smooth, distinct finish line.

mcqs.q: A sectioned silicone index is used during preparation to:
opts: Verify that the planned occlusal and axial clearances have actually been achieved
Act as a matrix for the final cement
mcqs.explain: Made before preparation and sectioned afterwards, the index reveals the true reduction at each cusp and wall so under-reduction can be corrected before the impression.

mcqs.q: Under-reduction discovered on the index should be corrected:
opts: At the try-in of the casting
mcqs.explain: Correcting before the impression avoids a thin, weak casting or an over-contoured crown.

mcqs.q: Inadequate occlusal clearance in a cast crown most likely results in:
opts: A thin casting liable to perforation, or an over-contoured crown
mcqs.explain: Without space for the metal the technician must either thin the casting (risking perforation) or over-contour the crown.

mcqs.q: Why does the full metal crown allow 'modifying the axial tooth contour'?
opts: The casting can be shaped to create guiding planes, contours and rest seats
It is bonded rather than cemented
mcqs.explain: Because the whole axial surface is covered by the casting, contours can be altered — which is why it serves as a survey crown.

mcqs.q: Compared with partial coverage, the complete cast crown is:
opts: More retentive and resistant but more destructive
mcqs.explain: Full coverage gives greater retention and resistance at the cost of removing more tooth structure than a partial-coverage restoration.

mcqs.q: A supragingival margin is preferred for the chamfer mainly because it:
opts: Is easier to finish, impress and clean, and is kinder to the periodontium
Improves esthetics in the smile zone
mcqs.explain: Supragingival margins are more accessible for finishing, impression-taking, cementation clean-up and oral hygiene.

mcqs.q: Which is listed as a DISADVANTAGE of the full metal crown besides esthetics?
opts: Galvanic and thermal conductivity can occur
Greater wear of the opposing natural teeth than porcelain
mcqs.explain: It is also destructive compared with a partial-coverage crown.

mcqs.q: Compared with porcelain, the full metal crown causes:
opts: Less wear of the opposing natural teeth
More wear of the opposing natural teeth
The same wear of the opposing natural teeth
Wear only of the opposing restoration
mcqs.explain: This is one of its stated advantages, alongside superior strength and good margin adaptation.

mcqs.q: As a special consideration, the minimum clearance on a NON-functional (non-centric) cusp is:
mcqs.explain: The general criterion gives 1 mm on non-functional and 1.5 mm on functional cusps; 0.6 mm is the stated special-consideration minimum.

mcqs.q: The minimum chamfer width is 0.5 mm in a molar, and in a premolar it:
mcqs.explain: The chamfer should be smooth and distinct and allow approximately 0.5 mm of metal thickness at the margin.

mcqs.q: Which diamond is used for BULK occlusal and axial reduction and to cut the chamfer?
mcqs.explain: The finer-grit round-end tapered diamond finishes the axial walls and margin; the short needle diamond gives proximal access.

mcqs.q: In the preparation sequence, occlusal reduction (step 2) is performed by:
opts: Joining the depth-orientation grooves while preserving the anatomic contour
Flattening the occlusal table to a single plane
Cutting the functional cusp bevel first
mcqs.explain: The grooves of step 1 are cut into the inclined planes following the normal anatomy, so that the reduction can be measured and controlled.

mcqs.q: The final step of the complete cast crown preparation is to:
opts: Round all line angles and refine the smooth, distinct supragingival chamfer
Break the proximal contact with the needle diamond
mcqs.explain: Rounding the line angles minimises stress concentration and cement failure.

mcqs.q: To verify the reduction with a silicone index, the index is:
opts: Made before preparation and sectioned bucco-lingually afterwards, then seated over the preparation
Made after preparation and compared with the opposing arch
Made from the impression material used for the final impression
Sectioned mesio-distally and seated on the adjacent teeth
mcqs.explain: The gap between index and tooth shows the actual reduction at each cusp and wall, so under-reduction is corrected before the impression.

saqs.q: List the advantages and disadvantages of the full metal crown.
saqs.a: ADVANTAGES — conservative among full crowns · superior strength · more retention and resistance · allows modification of axial contour · can serve as a survey crown · good margin adaptation · less wear of opposing natural teeth than porcelain. DISADVANTAGES — poor esthetics · destructive compared with partial coverage · possible galvanic and thermal conductivity.

saqs.q: State the indications and contraindications for a full metal crown.
saqs.a: INDICATIONS — extensive coronal destruction · maximum retention and resistance needed (bridge retainer, short clinical crown) · an uncorrectable inclined tooth · a survey crown with an occlusal rest seat · after root-canal treatment · as a bridge retainer. CONTRAINDICATIONS — esthetics is the patient's main concern · the objectives can be met more conservatively.

saqs.q: Give the reduction criteria (all dimensions) for a complete cast crown preparation.
saqs.a: OCCLUSAL — minimum clearance 1 mm non-functional, 1.5 mm functional (absolute minimum 0.6 mm non-functional), following normal anatomic contours. AXIAL — allow a 6° taper. MARGIN — a chamfer, ideally supragingival, smooth and distinct, giving ~0.5 mm of metal at the margin, minimum chamfer width 0.5 mm in a molar (less in a premolar). Plus a functional (centric) cusp bevel.

Criterion

a chamfer, ideally supragingival — smooth and distinct, allowing about 0.5 mm of metal thickness; minimum chamfer width 0.5 mm in a molar, less in a premolar

saqs.q: List the armamentarium and outline the step-by-step preparation sequence.
saqs.a: ARMAMENTARIUM — a round-end tapered diamond, a finer-grit round-end tapered diamond for finishing, and a short needle diamond. SEQUENCE — occlusal depth grooves on the inclined planes · join them, preserving contour (1 mm non-functional, 1.5 mm functional) · place the functional cusp bevel · axial reduction at ~6° carrying the chamfer · proximal reduction with the needle diamond · finish by rounding line angles and refining a smooth supragingival chamfer.

list: A second, finer-grit round-end tapered diamond for finishing

steps: Cut occlusal depth-orientation grooves into the inclined planes, following normal anatomy
Complete the occlusal reduction by joining the grooves — preserving anatomic contour, 1 mm non-functional and 1.5 mm functional
Axial reduction of buccal and lingual walls at about 6° convergence, carrying the chamfer as you go
Proximal reduction with the short needle diamond — break contact without damaging the adjacent tooth
Finish — round all line angles and refine a smooth, distinct, ideally supragingival chamfer

saqs.q: Explain how a silicone index is used to verify the preparation, and why this matters.
saqs.a: A putty index is made over the tooth BEFORE preparation and sectioned, usually bucco-lingually. Seating it over the preparation shows the gap between index and tooth — the actual reduction achieved at each cusp and axial wall — so under-reduction can be corrected before the final impression. It matters because inadequate clearance forces the technician either to make the casting too thin (perforation, distortion) or to over-contour the crown, compromising function and periodontal health.

saqs.q: State the reduction criteria for a complete cast crown preparation, including the special considerations.
saqs.a: OCCLUSAL — 1 mm non-functional, 1.5 mm functional, following anatomic contours. AXIAL — a 6° taper. MARGIN — chamfer, ideally supragingival, smooth and distinct, ~0.5 mm of metal. SPECIAL — a functional (centric) cusp bevel, wide, giving bulk of metal where the occlusal load is greatest; minimum 0.6 mm clearance on the non-functional cusp; minimum chamfer width 0.5 mm in a molar, less in a premolar.
